title: rorca-distribution
_notes: Standalone binary distribution via bun build --compile. No source visible, no runtime dependency. Postgres downloaded on first run (Prisma/Playwright pattern). 10 stories, 4 waves. Prerequisite: rorca-postgres-migration (replaces better-sqlite3 with pg). No Docker, no npm publish.
_prerequisite: rorca-postgres-migration must be completed first — replaces better-sqlite3 (native C++ addon) with pg (pure JS), eliminating the only native addon risk for bun build --compile

_architecture.binary: bun build --compile — standalone binary per platform, no source visible
_architecture.database: Postgres 16 + pgvector + AGE, downloaded on first run to ~/.rorca/postgres/
_architecture.install: curl -fsSL https://get.rorca.app | sh (macOS/Linux), irm https://get.rorca.app/install.ps1 | iex (Windows)
_architecture.port: Postgres on 5433 (avoids conflict with user's own 5432), Express on 3030

rejected_options.npm_publish: Source code visible in node_modules — violates no-source requirement
rejected_options.pglite_wasm: Single-connection lock blocks concurrent DB access — prevents real-time inspection during pipeline runs
rejected_options.docker: Deferred to separate spec — not needed for initial distribution
rejected_options.better-sqlite3: Native C++ addon breaks bun build --compile — requires postgres migration first

userStories.title: Postgres Binary Download Manager
userStories.description: Create backend/src/lib/postgres-manager.ts that manages downloading pre-built PostgreSQL 16 binaries (with pgvector and AGE extensions) on first run. Uses the same pattern as Prisma (downloads engine binaries to a cache dir) and Playwright (downloads browser binaries). On first rorca start, detect OS (darwin/linux/win32) and arch (arm64/x64), download the correct pre-built Postgres tarball from GitHub Releases to ~/.rorca/postgres/, extract it, and verify the binary works. Cache across runs — only re-download on version mismatch. Show download progress bar in terminal using a simple ASCII progress indicator.
acceptanceCriteria: New file backend/src/lib/postgres-manager.ts exports PostgresManager class with methods: download(), isInstalled(), getVersion(), getBinPath()
PostgresManager.download() detects process.platform (darwin/linux/win32) and process.arch (arm64/x64) to select correct binary
Downloads tarball from configurable POSTGRES_DOWNLOAD_URL (default: GitHub Releases URL for rorca-postgres-builds repo)
Extracts tarball to ~/.rorca/postgres/ preserving bin/, lib/, share/ directory structure
PostgresManager.isInstalled() returns true if ~/.rorca/postgres/bin/postgres exists and is executable
PostgresManager.getVersion() runs ~/.rorca/postgres/bin/postgres --version and parses output
Version mismatch triggers re-download: stored version in ~/.rorca/postgres/.version compared to expected POSTGRES_VERSION constant
Download progress shown in terminal: 'Downloading PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector... ████████████ 100% (52MB)'
If download fails (network error, 404): clear error message with manual download instructions as fallback
Supports 4 platform targets: darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, win32-x64
npx tsc --noEmit passes in backend/

userStories.title: Postgres Lifecycle Management (init, start, stop)
userStories.description: Add lifecycle management to PostgresManager: initialize database cluster on first run, start/stop Postgres server, create rorca database, and run migrations. Postgres runs on port 5433 (not 5432) to avoid conflicts with any Postgres the user already has installed. The lifecycle is tied to rorca start/stop — when Rorca starts, Postgres starts; when Rorca stops (Ctrl+C or SIGTERM), Postgres stops cleanly.
acceptanceCriteria: PostgresManager.initCluster() runs initdb to create cluster at ~/.rorca/data/ if not already initialized
PostgresManager.start() runs pg_ctl start with -D ~/.rorca/data/ -o '-p 5433' and waits for ready
PostgresManager.stop() runs pg_ctl stop with -D ~/.rorca/data/ -m fast for clean shutdown
PostgresManager.createDatabase() runs createdb rorca if database doesn't exist yet
PostgresManager.isRunning() checks pg_isready on port 5433
Port 5433 used by default (configurable via RORCA_PG_PORT env var) to avoid conflict with user's own Postgres on 5432
On process SIGINT (Ctrl+C): stop Postgres before exiting — register handler in bin/rorca.ts
On process SIGTERM: same graceful shutdown
If port 5433 is already in use: check if it's our managed Postgres (check pid file) — if yes, reuse; if no, error with clear message
Health check: PostgresManager.waitForReady(timeoutMs=30000) polls pg_isready every 500ms, throws if timeout
After Postgres is ready: set DATABASE_URL=postgresql://localhost:5433/rorca in process.env for pg Pool connection
Migrations run automatically after database creation via existing migration runner
All Postgres stdout/stderr logged to ~/.rorca/postgres.log (not mixed with Rorca output)
npx tsc --noEmit passes in backend/

userStories.title: Postgres Binary Build Pipeline
userStories.description: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that builds PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector and Apache AGE extensions from source for all 4 target platforms. The built binaries are published as release assets on a separate rorca-postgres-builds repository. This workflow runs manually (workflow_dispatch) or when the POSTGRES_VERSION is bumped. Each platform build produces a self-contained tarball with postgres, initdb, pg_ctl, pg_isready, createdb binaries plus pgvector.so and age.so extensions.
acceptanceCriteria: New file .github/workflows/build-postgres.yml with workflow_dispatch trigger
Matrix strategy builds for: macos-14 (arm64), macos-13 (x64), ubuntu-22.04 (x64), windows-2022 (x64)
Each build: clone postgres 16.x, configure with --prefix, make, make install
pgvector extension built from source (pgvector/pgvector repo) and installed into build prefix
Apache AGE extension built from source (apache/age repo) and installed into build prefix
Output tarball per platform: rorca-postgres-{platform}-{arch}.tar.gz containing bin/, lib/, share/
Tarballs uploaded as release assets with tag matching POSTGRES_VERSION (e.g. pg-16.4-v1)
Windows build uses MSVC toolchain (or MinGW if MSVC proves problematic)
Total tarball size per platform < 80MB (stripped binaries)
README in rorca-postgres-builds repo documents the build process and how to update Postgres version

userStories.title: Bun Build Compile — Proof of Concept
userStories.description: Run bun build --compile against the Rorca codebase to produce a standalone binary. With the postgres migration complete (better-sqlite3 replaced by pg), there are no native C++ addons — the entire codebase is pure TypeScript/JavaScript. Verify the compiled binary can: start Express, serve the static frontend, connect to the managed Postgres instance, run migrations, and pass a health check. This is the critical validation that bun compile works for Rorca.
acceptanceCriteria: bun build --compile bin/rorca.ts --outfile rorca produces a working binary on macOS arm64
Binary size is < 100MB (Bun runtime + Rorca app + frontend assets)
Running ./rorca --version prints correct version from package.json
Running ./rorca start starts Express server on port 3030 with RORCA_SERVE_STATIC=1
Static frontend (dist/) is served at / — browser shows Rorca UI
Backend connects to Postgres on 5433 (managed by DIST-002) and runs migrations
curl http://localhost:3030/api/health returns 200 with valid JSON
curl http://localhost:3030/api/workspaces returns 200 (proves DB connection works)
No source code extractable from the binary (verify: strings rorca | grep -c 'import ' shows minimal hits)
Frontend assets (HTML, JS, CSS) embedded in binary — no external dist/ folder needed
If bun compile fails on any import: document the issue and fix (likely path resolution or dynamic require)

userStories.title: LICENSE & Legal Files
userStories.description: Add a Business Source License 1.1 (BSL-1.1) file to the repository. BSL is the standard source-available license used by companies like HashiCorp (Terraform), MariaDB, CockroachDB, and Sentry. It allows viewing source code but restricts commercial hosting/resale. After a specified change date (typically 3-4 years), the code converts to a permissive license (Apache 2.0 or similar).
acceptanceCriteria: LICENSE file created at repository root with BSL-1.1 text
License header includes: Licensor (Rorca), Licensed Work (Rorca vX.X), Additional Use Grant (non-production use allowed), Change Date (4 years from initial release), Change License (Apache 2.0)
package.json license field updated to 'BSL-1.1'
backend/package.json license field updated to 'BSL-1.1'
LICENSE file shipped alongside binary in release archives (zip/tarball)
No NOTICE file needed (BSL-1.1 doesn't require it unless using Apache-licensed dependencies)

userStories.title: GitHub Actions — Release Workflow
userStories.description: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that automatically builds and releases Rorca binaries when a version tag is pushed. On git tag v*, the workflow: runs typecheck and tests, builds all 4 platform binaries, creates a GitHub Release with auto-generated release notes from conventional commits, and attaches the binaries as release assets.
acceptanceCriteria: New file .github/workflows/release.yml triggered on push tags: 'v*'
Step 1: checkout + setup bun + setup node
Step 2: npm ci && cd backend && npm ci (install dependencies)
Step 3: npx tsc --noEmit && cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit (typecheck both)
Step 4: cd backend && npm test (run tests)
Step 5: npm run build (frontend build)
Step 6: matrix build — 4 parallel jobs producing platform binaries via scripts/build-binaries.sh
Step 7: create GitHub Release using gh release create $TAG with --generate-notes flag
Step 8: upload all 4 binaries + LICENSE as release assets
Release title format: 'Rorca v{version}'
Release notes auto-generated from conventional commits since last tag (feat:, fix:, etc.)
Workflow has permissions: contents: write (for creating releases)
Workflow uses ubuntu-latest for Linux build, macos-14 for macOS ARM64, macos-13 for macOS x64

userStories.title: First-Run Experience
userStories.description: When a user runs rorca start for the first time (no ~/.rorca/ directory exists), provide a polished onboarding experience: show a welcome banner, download Postgres if needed, initialize the database, run migrations, start Express, and open the browser to the onboarding flow. Subsequent runs skip all setup steps and start in ~2 seconds. Update bin/rorca.ts to orchestrate this flow.
acceptanceCriteria: On first run (no ~/.rorca/ directory): create ~/.rorca/, ~/.rorca/data/, ~/.rorca/logs/
Show ASCII welcome banner with Rorca name and version
Step 1: Check if Postgres is installed (PostgresManager.isInstalled()) — if not, download it (DIST-001) with progress bar
Step 2: Initialize Postgres cluster if needed (PostgresManager.initCluster()) — show 'Initializing database cluster... done'
Step 3: Start Postgres (PostgresManager.start()) — show 'Starting PostgreSQL on port 5433... done'
Step 4: Create database + run migrations — show 'Running migrations (N tables)... done'
Step 5: Start Express on port 3030 — show 'Starting Rorca on http://localhost:3030'
If port 3030 is taken: try 3031, 3032, etc. up to 3039, then fail with clear message
Auto-open browser to http://localhost:{port} (use open on macOS, xdg-open on Linux, start on Windows)
Show 'Press Ctrl+C to stop.' at the end
Subsequent runs (~/. rorca/ exists, Postgres cluster initialized): skip download + init, start Postgres + Express directly in ~2s
All setup output uses consistent formatting: step descriptions left-aligned, status right-aligned (... done / ... failed)
If any step fails: show error with suggestion, don't proceed to next step

userStories.title: End-to-End Binary Smoke Test
userStories.description: Create a CI smoke test that verifies the compiled binary works end-to-end: download it, start it, verify health, verify frontend serves, verify DB connection, then clean up. This test runs on every PR that touches bin/, backend/, or the build scripts, catching regressions before release.
acceptanceCriteria: New file scripts/smoke-test.sh that runs the full verification
Step 1: Build binary (bun build --compile bin/rorca.ts --outfile ./build/rorca-test)
Step 2: Run ./build/rorca-test --version — verify exit code 0 and version output matches package.json
Step 3: Start ./build/rorca-test start --port 0 in background (random available port)
Step 4: Wait for health check (poll /api/health every 1s, timeout 60s — includes Postgres download on first CI run)
Step 5: curl /api/health returns 200 with JSON containing status: 'ok'
Step 6: curl / returns 200 with HTML containing '<div id="root">' (frontend serves)
Step 7: curl /api/workspaces returns 200 with JSON array (DB connected)
Step 8: Send SIGTERM to background process, verify clean shutdown (Postgres stopped)
Step 9: Verify ~/.rorca/data/ exists (cluster was created)
Step 10: Clean up — rm -rf ~/.rorca/ build/rorca-test
Exit code 0 on all passes, non-zero on any failure with descriptive error
New GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/smoke-test.yml — runs on PRs touching bin/**, backend/**, scripts/build-*
npm run test:smoke added to root package.json scripts
